questions.solution:
Arguments of f are evaluated right to left:
- h(20) first [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] prints 20
- then g(10) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] prints 10

Inside f(10, 20):
- g(x) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] prints 10
- h(y) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] prints 20

Output: 20101020

Answer: 20101020

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow

Each iteration does [latex]x\leftarrow2x+y[/latex], repeated [latex]y[/latex] times. Solving:
[latex]f(x,y)=2^y x+(2^y-1)y=2^y(x+y)-y[/latex]

- [latex]x=20,y=10[/latex]: [latex]1024\times30-10=30710[/latex]. This is less than [latex]2^{20}[/latex] but more than [latex]2^{10}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] options 1 and 3 FALSE.
- [latex]x=20,y=20[/latex]: [latex]2^{20}\times40-20 \gt 2^{20}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] TRUE.
- [latex]x=10,y=20[/latex]: [latex]2^{20}\times30-20 \gt 2^{20}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] TRUE.
(Both values are about [latex]4\times10^7[/latex], so no int overflow.)

questions.solution:
Each call of fX() reads one character and, if it is not newline, calls fX() again before printing. Each call has its own local [latex]a[/latex].

Calls read: '1' [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] '2' [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] '3' [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] '4' [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] '\n'. The last call reads newline, makes no further call and prints nothing.

While returning, the calls print their characters in reverse order: 4, 3, 2, 1. Then main returns normally.

Answer: The program will terminate with 4321 as output

questions.solution:
Integer division is used.

Iteration 1: [latex]a=6/12+1=0+1=1[/latex], then [latex]a=a+b=1+0=1[/latex].
Iteration 2: [latex]a=1/12+1=0+1=1[/latex] again, and so on.

[latex]a[/latex] is stuck at 1, so the condition [latex]a \lt 10[/latex] is always true and printf is never reached.

questions.solution:
Trace the calls:
- main calls f1(), f2(2), f3() [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3 children.
- f2(2) calls f3(), then since X [latex]\ne[/latex] 1, calls f2(1).
- f2(1) calls f3(), then since X == 1, calls f1().

Tree: main [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {f1, f2, f3}; f2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {f3, f2}; inner f2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] {f3, f1}. This matches (A).

Answer: A
